title: Integrated Transcriptomic and Targeted Metabolomic Analyses Elucidate the Molecular Mechanism Underlying Dihydromyricetin Synthesis in Nekemias grossedentata.
authors: Wu, Fuwen; Feng, Zhi; Yao, Zhi; Zhang, Peiling; Wang, Yiqiang; Li, Meng
one_liner_zh: 该文通过转录组和代谢组分析鉴定DHM合成关键基因NgF3'5'H3和NgMYB71，并做分子对接，但核心是植物代谢通路而非蛋白质-DNA互作，仅分子对接涉及蛋白-小分子，与TF-DNA结合机制无关。
abstract: Nekemias grossedentata (Hand.-Mazz.) J. Wen & Z. L. Nie is a medicinal and edible plant with a high dihydromyricetin (DHM) content in its bud tips. Vine tea made from its bud tips has served as a health tea and Chinese herbal medicine for nearly 700 years. However, the molecular mechanisms underlying the high DHM content in N. grossedentata bud tips remain inadequately elucidated. This study conducted qualitative and quantitative analyses of bud tip flavonoids utilizing HPLC and targeted metabolomics. Core genes influencing the substantial synthesis of DHM in N. grossedentata were identified through integrated transcriptome and metabolome analyses. The results revealed that 65 flavonoid metabolites were detected in bud tips, with DHM as the predominant flavonoid (37.5%), followed by myricetin (0.144%) and taxifolin (0.141%). Correlation analysis revealed a significant positive correlation between NgF3'5'H3 expression and DHM content. Co-expression analysis and qRT-PCR validation demonstrated a significant positive correlation between NgMYB71 and NgF3'5'H3, with consistent expression trends across three periods and four tissues. Consequently, NgF3'5'H3 and NgMYB71 were identified as core genes influencing the substantial synthesis of DHM in N. grossedentata. Elevated NgMYB71 expression in bud tips induced high NgF3'5'H3 expression, facilitating extensive DHM synthesis in bud tips. Molecular docking analysis revealed that NgF3'5'H3 had a strong binding affinity for taxifolin. NgF3'5'H3 was the pivotal core node gene in the dihydromyricetin biosynthesis pathway in N. grossedentata and was highly expressed in bud tips. The strong specific binding of NgF3'5'H3 to dihydromyricetin precursor metabolites catalyzed their conversion into DHM, resulting in higher DHM contents in bud tips than in other tissues or plants. This study aimed to elucidate the molecular mechanisms underlying the substantial synthesis of DHM in N. grossedentata, providing a theoretical foundation for enhancing DHM production and developing N. grossedentata resources.
abstract_zh: Nekemias grossedentata (Hand.-Mazz.) J. Wen & Z. L. Nie是一种药食两用植物，其嫩芽尖端含有高含量的二氢杨梅素（dihydromyricetin, DHM）。以其嫩芽尖制成的藤茶作为保健茶和中草药已有近700年的历史。然而，N. grossedentata嫩芽尖中高DHM含量的分子机制尚未得到充分阐明。本研究利用高效液相色谱（HPLC）和靶向代谢组学对嫩芽尖黄酮类化合物进行了定性和定量分析。通过转录组和代谢组联合分析，鉴定了影响N. grossedentata中DHM大量合成的核心基因。结果显示，在嫩芽尖中检测到65种黄酮类代谢物，其中DHM为主要黄酮类化合物（37.5%），其次是杨梅素（myricetin）（0.144%）和花旗松素（taxifolin）（0.141%）。相关性分析显示，NgF3'5'H3表达与DHM含量呈显著正相关。共表达分析和qRT-PCR验证表明，NgMYB71与NgF3'5'H3之间存在显著正相关，且在三个时期和四种组织中的表达趋势一致。因此，NgF3'5'H3和NgMYB71被确定为影响N. grossedentata中DHM大量合成的核心基因。嫩芽尖中NgMYB71表达升高诱导了NgF3'5'H3的高表达，促进了嫩芽尖中DHM的大量合成。分子对接分析显示，NgF3'5'H3对花旗松素具有强结合亲和力。NgF3'5'H3是N. grossedentata中二氢杨梅素生物合成途径的关键核心节点基因，并在嫩芽尖中高表达。NgF3'5'H3与二氢杨梅素前体代谢物的强特异性结合催化其转化为DHM，导致嫩芽尖中DHM含量高于其他组织或植物。本研究旨在阐明N. grossedentata中DHM大量合成的分子机制，为提高DHM产量和开发N. grossedentata资源提供理论基础。
